title: Multi-tenant tagging & dashboard composition for inference
content:
Purpose
This note captures a lightweight, actionable taxonomy and dashboard composition pattern for multi-tenant inference telemetry. Goal: make dashboards and traces sliceable by tenant, product, model-variant, and routing-policy without exploding cardinality or losing signal. Intended audience: dashboard owners, backend/serving engineers, SRE, product analytics.

Problem statement
- We run inference for many customers (tenants) and internal products. Teams want per-tenant SLOs and the ability to correlate regressions with model variants, autoscale events, and fallback behavior.
- Naively tagging every metric by tenant + route + model + instance_type leads to cardinality explosion and slow query performance.
- Current dashboards duplicate the same widgets per-tenant or use heavyweight filtered dashboards that are hard to maintain.

Design principles (prioritized)
1) Low-cardinality primary keys: keep most metrics tagged by coarse buckets (env, cluster, model_family) and capture tenant/model specifics in a small set of additional labels that are optional or sampled.
2) Slice-on-demand: collect high-cardinality attributes in traces or sampled logs rather than full-metric tags; use joinable identifiers to correlate later.
3) Persona-first dashboards: compose small reusable panels (widgets) and expose per-tenant filters at runtime rather than prebuilding one dashboard per tenant.
4) Signal preservation: ensure critical SLI metrics for latency, error-rate, and cost-per-token are always available at full resolution (no sampling).

Tagging taxonomy (recommended keys)
- service: inference-runtime | gateway | cache-service (low cardinality)
- env: prod | staging | dev
- region: e.g., us-west1
- shard: e.g., gpool-1 (infrastructure shard)
- model_family: gpt-family | llama-family (coarse model grouping)
- model_version: rwi-3b-v1 | open-7b-q4 (moderate cardinality; required for model rollouts)
- tenant_id: redwood-corp | acme (HIGH cardinality — should be used sparingly)
- route: text-generate | chat | embeddings (low cardinality)
- policy: primary | fallback | burst (low cardinality)
- sampling_key: a deterministic hash used to identify a sampled request across metrics/traces (keeps metrics low-cardinality; see sampling section)

Notes on tenant_id and cardinality
- tenant_id is useful for per-customer billing and SLAs. Do NOT attach tenant_id to every aggregate metric. Instead:
  - Keep core SLI counters (requests_total, tokens_consumed_total, errors_total) tagged by env, region, route, model_family, and policy (no tenant_id).
  - Emit tenant-level counters as a separate metric series with a different retention policy and ingestion pipeline (e.g., tenant_requests_total) that is rate-limited or aggregated at agent side (see client-side aggregator below).
  - Alternatively, emit tenant metrics to a high-cardinality store (e.g., ClickHouse/BigQuery) rather than Prometheus; use scheduled pipelines to populate per-tenant rollups in Prometheus-friendly metrics.

Sampling and join strategy
- Introduce sampling_key (deterministic 128-bit hex string) generated at request ingress. Attach sampling_key to:
  - a small fraction (1–5%) of full-resolution metrics as an additional label,
  - every trace/span and selected logs for that request.
- Use the sampling_key to join traces to sampled metric series in offline analysis or ad-hoc dashboards. This keeps Prometheus cardinality low while retaining the ability to debug tenant-specific incidents.

Traces and span design guidance
- Required spans: http_ingress -> auth_check -> routing -> model_invoke -> kv_cache_lookup* -> tokenizer -> response_serialize
- Key attributes to include on spans (prefer in trace attributes, not metric labels): tenant_id, model_version, route, policy, selected_backend (gpu_id or pool), kv_cache_hit=true/false, batch_size, seq_len
- Sampling rules: always sample traces for requests that hit an alerting threshold (e.g., latency > SLA*1.5 or error). For regular traffic, sample ~2% uniformly plus heavy sampling for large batch_size or long seq_len to detect tail behavior.

Dashboard composition pattern
- Base dashboard (global view): high-level aggregated widgets with filters for env/region/model_family/route. Do NOT expose tenant filter here. Widgets: 99th/95th/50th latency (per-route), requests/s, errors/s, tokens/s, cost_per_token estimate, active_unseen_fallbacks (count of requests that went to fallback policy).
- Tenant drilldown template: parametric dashboard that accepts tenant_id as a variable and pulls from the tenant-level metrics pipeline or joins traces by sampling_key. For multi-tenant customers, enable a URL builder that sets tenant variable.
- Per-team quick-dashboard (persona-driven): preconfigured composition for SRE (latency/error heatmaps), model-owner (quality: perplexity/regression eval hooks + request examples), billing (tokens & cost), and solutions-engineering (tail traces + recent logs).
- Reusable panels library: store every panel as a JSON snippet keyed by metric_name + primary_tags; compose dashboards programmatically so updates propagate. Avoid copy-paste dashboards.

Example panels and PromQL hints (conceptual)
- Global 95p latency per route:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Requests/s (core metric, no tenant):
  sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (env, region, route, policy)
- Tenant requests (from high-card store/rollup): use external data source or expose rollup metric tenant_requests_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"} for tenant dashboards

Alerting recommendations
- Keep alert rules on low-cardinality core SLIs (prod env only):
  - SLO latency burn rate alert: if request_latency_p50/95 error budget burn > X over 30m
  - Error spike: increase in errors/s by 3x over 5m relative to baseline
- Tenant-specific alerts should be implemented as part of customer-facing SLA layer (not global infra alerts) and routed to account owner on rotation.
- Add an automated trace-capture for top-n slow requests when SLO breaches to accelerate RCA.

Operational runbook snippets
- When a tenant reports high latency:
  1) Open tenant drilldown dashboard and confirm requests/s and latency trends.
  2) Check routing.policy counters: are fallbacks increasing?
  3) Look at sampled traces (search by tenant_id or sampling_key) for kv_cache_hit=false, long model_invoke spans, or large batch sizes.
  4) If model_version change correlates, roll back to previous canary.

Implementation checklist (phased)
- Phase 1 (quick wins):
  - Standardize metric names and low-cardinality labels across services.
  - Implement sampling_key on ingress and propagate to traces and logs.
  - Create base dashboard and reusable panel library.
- Phase 2 (tenant pipeline):
  - Add agent-side tenant aggregator that emits tenant-level rollups to a long-term store.
  - Build tenant drilldown template dashboard that consumes rollups.
- Phase 3 (quality + rollout):
  - Integrate with cost attribution and billing pipelines.
  - Add alert-to-owner automation for tenant SLA breaches.

Migration notes and pitfalls
- Do not backfill tenant_id onto historical metrics in Prometheus; instead produce rollups from raw logs/traces to avoid cardinality shock.
- Beware dashboards that use template variables with high-cardinality values (e.g., tenant_id dropdown with 10k entries). Use a search-as-you-type flow or a URL parameter instead.
- Monitor metric ingestion cardinality post-rollout for any unexpected label expansion. Build a guard that rejects metrics with new label values above a threshold.

Ownership and rollout plan
- Obs owners: eng-observability (Asha Patel lead), serving-runtime instrumentation (Jing Wu), SRE (Samir Khan)
- Roadmap: prototype sampling and panel library (Q4 2024), tenant rollups POC (Q1 2025), GA dashboards + alerts (Q2 2025).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Acceptable sampling rate tradeoff for traces vs debugging speed — propose 2% uniform + priority sampling for errors and large batches.
- Which long-term store will host tenant rollups? (ClickHouse vs BigQuery) Cost/latency tradeoffs to be evaluated.

Appendix: quick glossary
- rollup: aggregated metric series for a specific dimension (e.g., tenant) computed upstream to avoid cardinality in the real-time store.
- sampling_key: deterministic id used to correlate metrics/traces without tagging all metrics with high-cardinality labels.
- panel library: collection of small reusable dashboard widgets that can be composed into multiple dashboards.

Action items
- [Asha] Draft schema for tenant rollup metric names and retention (due 2024-11-17).
- [Diego] Implement sampling_key at gateway and add to traces (PR by 2024-12-01).
- [Jing] Build reusable panel library and base dashboard (by 2024-12-15).

Comments welcome — drop feedback in #obs-instrumentation or edit the Confluence spec linked above.
